headline: How an HVAC Company Scaled to ~396 Meta Ads Leads a Month
summary_line: PPC Guru launched EcoCare's Meta Ads program and grew it into a dependable lead engine for home-comfort services — from 32 lead-form enquiries in the first month (Aug 2025) to roughly 396 genuine leads a month in the most recent complete quarter (Apr–Jun 2026), at about $26 per lead across furnaces, heat pumps and water heaters.
client_context: EcoCare is a home-comfort and HVAC services provider serving homeowners across Ontario, Canada, including the Greater Toronto Area and Ottawa. The business installs and services furnaces, heat pumps, air conditioners, tankless and traditional water heaters, water treatment systems and EV chargers. Demand for these services is high-intent and often seasonal, and homeowners increasingly research and enquire on Facebook and Instagram. Meta Ads lets EcoCare reach those homeowners with the right offer at the right time and capture their contact details directly through lead forms, which makes reliable lead measurement central to the account's growth.
background: EcoCare partnered with PPC Guru to build a Meta Ads lead-generation program from the ground up. Rather than a takeover of an existing account, this was a launch: PPC Guru stood up the campaign structure, lead forms and tracking, then grew spend in step with proven results. The first full month of delivery was August 2025, and the program has run continuously since.
analysis: The plan treated Meta as a direct lead channel rather than an awareness play. Early testing in the first weeks compared messaging and engagement approaches against lead forms; lead forms won on both volume and cost, so budget was concentrated there. From there the account was built service by service — water heaters, furnaces and heat pumps, air conditioners, water treatment and EV chargers — so each offer could be measured on its own cost per lead and scaled independently.
analysis_points: Launch Instant Form lead campaigns so homeowner enquiries are captured directly in-platform.
Split campaigns by service line (water heaters, furnaces/heat pumps, AC, water treatment, EV chargers) to measure cost per lead per offer.
Use Campaign Budget Optimization so spend flows to the best-performing service and audience automatically.
Scale budget only as cost per lead held steady, month over month.

About 84 leads a month on average as service-line campaigns and audiences were established.

577 lead-form enquiries in a single month at about $29 each, the strongest month on record.

challenge: EcoCare needed a predictable flow of new-customer enquiries for a wide range of home-comfort services, in a competitive Ontario market and against seasonal demand swings. Starting from a new Meta Ads program meant proving, service by service, that Facebook and Instagram could deliver genuine leads at a cost that made sense before spend could safely be scaled.

changes.why: Captured homeowner name, phone and service interest directly in-platform, lowering friction versus sending cold traffic to a landing page.
Separate campaigns for water heaters, furnaces/heat pumps, AC, water treatment and EV chargers so each offer's cost per lead could be measured and scaled independently.
Let Meta shift budget toward the audiences and services producing the cheapest genuine leads.
Continuously tested hooks and intro offers per service to keep cost per lead down as spend grew.
Re-engaged people who saw an ad or opened a form but did not submit, recovering additional leads.
Monthly budget was increased only as cost per lead held steady, so scaling added proportionally more genuine enquiries.

benchmark: Cost per lead rose modestly from about $19 in the launch month to about $26 in the most recent quarter, while monthly budget scaled roughly 17× — the added spend brought about 12× more genuine leads, so the account grew volume without losing cost efficiency at scale.

early_stage.title: The First 90 Days
early_stage.intro: The program proved itself quickly. The first full month (August 2025) delivered 32 lead-form enquiries at about $19 each. After a steady September, October marked the first real scale-up as service-line campaigns came online and monthly leads jumped past 100.

gradual: From launch, results compounded quarter over quarter rather than spiking once and fading. The account averaged about 84 leads a month in Q4 2025, climbed to about 191 a month in Q1 2026 as budget scaled on proven cost per lead, and reached about 396 genuine leads a month in Q2 2026 — peaking near 553 in June. July 2026 went further still, at 577 lead-form enquiries in a single month. The monthly trend below shows a steady, compounding climb with the natural month-to-month variation of a real account, not a one-off spike.

spotlight.title: Why Splitting Campaigns by Service Line Mattered
spotlight.body: Rather than running one broad HVAC campaign, PPC Guru built separate campaigns for water heaters, furnaces and heat pumps, air conditioners, water treatment and EV chargers. Each service has its own audience, seasonality and cost per lead, so measuring them separately let the account pour budget into whatever was performing that month and pull back on what was not. Water heaters and furnaces/heat pumps became the workhorses, together producing the majority of genuine leads, while offers like EV chargers filled demand gaps. That structure is what let spend scale roughly 17× without cost per lead running away.

lessons: Use in-platform lead forms to capture enquiries directly — every extra click to a landing page costs you leads.
Split campaigns by service line so you can measure and scale each offer on its own cost per lead.
Test messaging, engagement and lead objectives early, then concentrate budget on whatever produces genuine enquiries cheapest.
Scale budget only when cost per lead holds steady, so growth adds real leads rather than just impressions.
Keep a retargeting layer running to recover people who opened a form but did not submit.
why_it_worked: Instant Forms captured genuine homeowner enquiries in-platform, keeping cost per lead low.
A service-line campaign structure made every offer measurable and independently scalable.
Budget was scaled on proven cost per lead, so 17× the spend brought about 12× the leads.
Continuous creative and audience testing kept efficiency steady as volume grew.
outcome: Today EcoCare runs on a predictable, scalable Meta Ads lead engine. In the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026) the program generated about 396 genuine lead-form enquiries a month — peaking near 553 in June — at a cost around $26 per lead, and July 2026 pushed higher still to 577 in a single month. That is up from 32 enquiries in the launch month less than a year earlier. Because every dollar of spend is measured against genuine leads by service line, EcoCare scales its budget with confidence and has a clear, data-backed basis for continued growth across its home-comfort offering.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian home-services companies turn Facebook and Instagram into a predictable flow of genuine enquiries with conversion-focused Meta Ads and transparent reporting.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Meta Ads account and shown on a monthly and quarterly basis. 'Leads' are lead-form submissions (Instant Forms and website leads) counted by Meta's lead metric — messaging and awareness activity is excluded so counts reflect genuine enquiries. 'Now' is the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026); the launch month (August 2025) is the first full month under PPC Guru.
lead_quality: Leads are homeowner-submitted forms that include phone number and service interest, so the sales team can follow up directly on genuine home-comfort enquiries.
